US inflation has soared over the summer, reaching a three-year high of 4.2% in May before coming down to 3.4% in July andAugust.Stubbornly high prices set up a tough decision for the US Federal Reserve, which will on Wednesday announce any changes to the interest rate. The central bank is largely expected to raise rates for the first time since July 2023, which could help mitigate prices, though Donald Trump has demanded rates to be lowered.Explore more on these topicsUS economynewsShareReuse this content

title: Could AI really wipe out humanity – six experts spell out the risks | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
description: We examine claims and counterclaims about the risks and calls to slow down the pace of AI development
Author: Aisha Down
Headline: We examine claims and counterclaims about the risks and calls to slow down the pace of AI development
Content: Experts say claims AI could kill all humans through biological weapons development had no scientific basis.Illustration: wildpixel/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenExperts say claims AI could kill all humans through biological weapons development had no scientific basis.Illustration: wildpixel/Getty ImagesAI (artificial intelligence)ExplainerCould AI really wipe out humanity – six experts spell out the risksWe examine claims and counterclaims about the risks and calls to slow down the pace of AI developmentRobert Booth,Dan MilmoandAisha DownTue 15 Sep 2026 13.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 16.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere have been some shocking claims in recent days about AI safety: we face a 10% chance of doom; AIs are worse than nukes; a “botnet” threatens the entire internet; it’s all a big tech psyop.Below, we look at six claims and reactions to them.‘In 6–12 months … a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet – potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage’ – Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, 12 September 2026Amodei’s concerns should not be entirely dismissed but require a large shaker of salt, said Gary Marcus, an AI sceptic and emeritus professor at New York University.It was “nonsensical”, he said, to suggest the entire internet is vulnerable and that it was “pretty unclear how that happens without extreme negligence on the part of the labs themselves”. Marcus highlighted a recent assessment by theUK AI Security Institutethat Mythos, one of Anthropic’s current leading-edge AIs, could “autonomously compromise [only] small, weakly defended vulnerable systems”.With large parts of the internet driven by computer infrastructure owned by Cloudflare, Google and Amazon Web Services(AWS), Marcus – assessing the claim with two colleagues – said he doubted that any of those companies could be taken down or controlled for a prolonged period of time without government force. Less defended individual websites might be attacked but “the internet itself is very unlikely to crumble”, they said.Meanwhile Niels Rogge, an engineer at Hugging Face which was hacked by OpenAI agents, called the internet takeover claim “bizarre nonsense”. The hack into Hugging Face resulted from improper human control and “an insane amount of compute only they can afford”, he said.Add to Amodei’s assessment of an internet takeover within a year the view expressed on Monday by his Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark, that the moment when AIs “start doing dangerous stuff” was in about 20 years, and the picture becomes more doubtful still.Prof Alan Woodward at the University of Surrey’s centre for cyber security said botnets tend to stall as the internet is not homogeneous and it is difficult to design them to persist in all its parts. Internet traffic is also resilient and tends to reroute around damage.“The AIs would not decide to do it on their own,” Woodward said. “It’s the humans that are responsible and the AI is a tool. That is what we need to control, not the AI.”‘We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade’ – Evan Hubinger, alignment science lead at Anthropic, 9 September 2026This statementis an expression of what is known in the AI world as p(doom) – or probability of doom. It’s the likelihood of AI wiping out humanity by evading our control and triggering catastrophe, perhaps through developing potent bioweapons or crashing the global financial system.One survey of researchers’ forecasts, published this week, asks them to place a number on the chance of “human extinction or similarly permanent and severe disempowerment from advanced AI”. But Heidy Khlaaf, chief scientist at the AI Now Institute research body, is among experts sceptical about giving percentage chances to existential scenarios.“These claims are neither falsifiable nor verifiable, making then unscientific by their very nature,” she said. The shortage of concrete examples of what a “superintelligent” AI might do to cause “doom” only adds to the cloudiness. A source familiar with Anthropic’s thinking acknowledges that “the exact chances of any one outcome are probably unknowable”.“If you cannot provide such evidence, it also implies whatever numbers you produced for ‘extinction’ have no scientific basis,” Khlaaf added. Critics say such numbers borrow the authority of science without doing the work.Even if quantifying risk is hard, there are qualitative examples of it. Safety incidents have happened and worst-outcome scenarios have been mooted. OpenAI confirmed in July that its agents – AI tools acting autonomously – hadgone rogue during a safety test. The agents colluded, communicated and strategised in a sophisticated “swarm” to hack into other parts of the internet.Meanwhile, on Monday, OpenAI researcher Dan Selsam said all-powerful AIs could trigger “runaway industrialisation that makes the planet inhospitable to humans”. Anthropic also said last week it found “five case studies of actors using our models in ways that could support biological weapons development”.'I think the groundwork for this psy op (for lack of a better term) has been prepared for a long time. This was just the match that lit the fire' – Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and the world’s richest person, 10 September 2026Musk’s reference to a “psy op” alludes to the argument that the big AI companies are calling for tighter regulation of the technology so that it effectively brings up the drawbridge on advanced AI. If governments putrestrictions on development of cutting-edge AI, can startups find the money and personnel to adhere to the regime?The US vice-president, JD Vance, on Monday said he felt “a little bit weird about the fact that you have so many frontier AI tech companies kind of coming to the government and begging the government to regulate them”. He said it felt like “a Trojan horse”.Anthropic’s Clark said governments should act while there is a small number of key players, so it is easier to put in place a “policy regime … that can prevent accidents and can prevent the technology spiralling out of control”. Critics call this a “regulatory capture” strategy on the assumption such regulation might slow down the progress of potential rivals.View image in fullscreenElon Musk, CEO of Anthropic Dario Amodei, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have said AI firms should slow down AI development.Composite: Fabrice Coffrini; Julien de Rosa; Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty ImagesOthers think Amodei’s risk warnings and calls for regulation and pacing are sincere. Yoshua Bengio, the Canadian computer scientist and a pioneer of modern AI , who has campaigned against breakneck AI development, said he is sceptical that this is an elaborate lobbying scheme. Applying the brakes is not in the interests of companies preparing for stock market flotations that could be worth trillions of dollars, he said.“If the governments impose what they’re asking for, which is pacing to avoid catastrophic risks, that’s going to cost them financially quite a lot,” he said.'A superintelligent AI poses a threat on the same, possibly, a greater scale' to nuclear weapons – Des Browne, former UK defence secretary, 7 September 2026“Unfortunately he is entirely correct,” said Toby Ord, senior researcher at Oxford University’s AI governance initiative. “Just as we can’t uninvent the bomb, once we develop AI systems that surpass humanity it would be almost impossible to go back.”But the key point is that superintelligent AI does not yet exist and is not guaranteed to happen. The safety-oriented AI Futures Projectforecastssuch a thing will not emerge before December 2028. OpenAI’s chief executive Sam Altman hassaidit could take until 2035.The Rand CorporationconcludedAI cannot cause the use of nuclear weapons because of strict safeguards built into their command and control systems. But this was based on assumptions including defence officials not introducing AI into the weapons’ management systems. The UN resolved in December that human control and oversight should be maintained over nuclear weapon control systems.AIs could contribute to other nuclear risks. AIs might use disinformation to influence the humans in charge – for example deceptively suggesting an adversary is about to launch a nuclear strike.The International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weaponswarns“cyber-attacks could manipulate the information decision-makers get to launch nuclear weapons, and interfere with the operation of nuclear weapons themselves”. It said AI could accelerate other aspects of warfare, squeezing the time for human decision-making.'You’ve got to be a moron not to say slow it down' – Bernie Sanders, Democrat senator for Vermont, 10 September 2026Sanders wants a ban on the creation of superintelligence and a pause on advanced AI development, citing AI industry leaders who say directly they are developing a dangerous technology.The most prominent opponent of a slowdown is Donald Trump, who responded to calls to do so this week saying the only guardrails needed are a “STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT”. Heclaimed there is a “sick conspiracy” against AI and datacentres“and the only one that is happy about it is China”.Pedro Domingos, emeritus professor of computer science at the University of Washington, is among accelerationists pushing for the research to keep going.“The path to better understanding and control of AI is more research, not less,” he has said. “What would be truly irresponsible is putting up barriers to it.”Alex Karp, the chief executive of Palantir, said: “If we didn’t have the adversaries we have, I would be very in favour of pausing this technology completely, but we do. You can’t pause it because it’s a structural advantage.”'There is no day after tomorrow if China wins at this. If they were to pull away from us on AI, then nothing else would matter' – Scott Bessent, US treasury secretary, 8 September 2026The US and China are runaway leaders in AI development. There is a view that ceding the lead to Beijing would be an irretrievable situation, so there can be no slowdown.This treats AI as if it were a super-weapon, equivalent to the nuclear arms buildout of the cold war, and AI models are machines of mass destruction, as opposed to a group of diverse technologies with broad applications.Amodei said “a Chinese lead in AI would pose grave danger for the US and the world”, but a Chinese government spokesperson responded that “fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance, which serves no one’s interest”.Some commentators see another motive for this the Washington/Anthropic framing of the China threat. An engineer who worked for Hugging FacesuggestedAmodei’s call for pacing the frontier comes from a desire to suppress the progress of cheap, open-source Chinese AI models.These models are nearly as capable as OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s, with the difference being that their source code is available to anyone and they do not charge their users. They pose a serious threat to Anthropic and OpenAI’s path to profitability, and there are hundreds of billions of dollars on the line.Explore more on these topicsAI (artificial intelligence)AnthropicEthicsSam AltmanElon MuskOpenAIDatacentresexplainersShareReuse this content

title: Panama canal traffic facing further cuts as drought from El Niño worsens | Panama canal | The Guardian
description: Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes
Author: Mark Saunokonoko
Headline: Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes
Content: A Liberian-flagged container ship transits the Panama canal. A lack of rainfall linked to El Niño has affected the water levels in the canal, resulting in officials reducing daily vessel traffic.Photograph: Enea Lebrun/ReutersView image in fullscreenA Liberian-flagged container ship transits the Panama canal. A lack of rainfall linked to El Niño has affected the water levels in the canal, resulting in officials reducing daily vessel traffic.Photograph: Enea Lebrun/ReutersPanama canalPanama canal traffic facing further cuts as drought from El Niño worsensPlanned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanesMark Saunokonokowith Agence France-PresseMon 14 Sep 2026 22.43 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 17.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThePanama canalplans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.From October, an average of 29.5 vessels will be allowed to transit daily – down 18% from 36 in August, according to a draft plan submitted to Panama’s parliament. In September, officials cut daily transits from 36 to 32 because of the drought.How Panama canal connects the Caribbean Sea to the Pacific OceanThe US and Israel’s war on Iran, and its disruption to the strait of Hormuz, has complicated logistics and added costs for shipping companies using the canal.In August, with vessels waiting 10 days to enter the canal – the longest since May – a container shipreportedly paid about $4m(£3m) to jump the queue. Maritime companies usually pay a flat fee to reserve a slot to transit the canal, but a daily auction allows shipowners to place bids to skip the queue. Bid prices generally rise during high demand.Shipping restrictions on the canal could yet worsen, with El Niño expected to peak later this year. The natural weather pattern that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns is forecast to be the strongest in four decades.The 82km-long canal, connecting the Caribbean Sea to the Pacific Ocean, relies on fresh water from rivers pouring into Lake Gatun to operate its system of locks. In September, officials said the watershed had received lower than forecast rainfall.The canal’s locks act like elevators, each filling with water to lift ships 26 metres (85 feet) from sea level to Lake Gatun and then back down to sea level on the other side.If lake levels are no longer safe for the largest ships to pass, the Panama Canal Authority imposes restrictions for safety and to preserve water.In 2023 the water level in the lakes feeding the canal was so low authorities cut daily transits from 38 to 22. Those restrictions led to a bottleneck of ships and sent companiesscrambling to find alternative routes.El Niño has severely affected Central America and northern parts of South America, where nine countries have experienced their hottest June-August period on record this year.Panama canal to reduce shipping as El Niño strikes vital routeRead moreFifty-two countries across all continents broke their seasonal temperature records for that period, according to an Agence France-Presse analysis of meteorological data from the European Copernicus programme.The extreme heat has taken many forms, fromunprecedented heatwaves in Europeto devastating drought in Sudan andtoxic smoke in Indonesia.More than a third of people experiencing the hottest northern summer months on record were in Africa, particularly in the Sahel and areas south of it.Eighteen African countries broke their seasonal records for the June-August period, from Mauritania and Sierra Leone in the west to Eritrea and Ethiopia in the east.Explore more on these topicsPanama canalPanamaAmericasEl Niño southern oscillationDroughtShipping industryInternational tradenewsShareReuse this content

title: Szoboszlai screamer seals Liverpool’s progress as De Zerbi’s Spurs woes grow | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Liverpool won the Carabao Cup third-round tie 3-1 against Tottenham via impressive strikes from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Liverpool won the Carabao Cup third-round tie 3-1 against Tottenham via impressive strikes from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai
Content: Dominik Szoboszlai salutes Anfield after his strike gave Liverpool a 3-1 lead in stoppage time.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersView image in fullscreenDominik Szoboszlai salutes Anfield after his strike gave Liverpool a 3-1 lead in stoppage time.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersCarabao CupSzoboszlai screamer seals Liverpool’s progress as De Zerbi’s Spurs woes growAndy Hunterat AnfieldTue 15 Sep 2026 17.12 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTottenham scored and Roberto De Zerbi eulogised the quality at his disposal, yet try telling Spurs’ suffering away support there was consolation to be found at Anfield.Liverpooltoyed with De Zerbi by advancing into round four with a quality of finishing that he can only dream of.While the Spurs head coach talked a good game and his players played a pretty one in harmless areas, Liverpool produced the only effective one. Alexis Mac Allister promoted his claims for a new contract forthe second midweek in successionwith an excellent strike and Cody Gakpo continued his fine early season form with a smart second plus an assist. But both were overshadowed by Dominik Szoboszlai’s stupendous 25-yard finish in stoppage time.Max Dowman doubles up for Arsenal’s back-ups to beat Ipswich in Carabao CupRead more“It was a worldie,” said Liverpool’s head coach, Andoni Iraola, whose changes injected energy and bite into the home display. “The thing with Dom is you trust him to score before he shoots. With others you might think it’s too far out, but not with him.”Spurs caused a few anxieties when Conor Gallagher headed home after Giorgi Mamardashvili’s failure to deal with a Mateus Fernandes corner. But the Liverpool stand-in keeper atoned with several impressive stops, the best from Omar Marmoush, and the visitors’ wastefulness would prove another factor in their downfall. Defeat was deserved, despite De ­Zerbi’s claims to the contrary.“We have to shoot more, we have to shoot better and we have to finish better the clear situations,” said the Spurs head coach. “But we are sorry for the result, disappointed, frustrated. I think it is unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments. In these five or six games we have not been lucky. We have to improve a lot of things but we are in the right way. I have big confidence and a big opinion of my players.”View image in fullscreenGiorgi Mamardashvili clutches the ball as Destiny Udogie runs by.Photograph: Jon Super/APDe Zerbi made eight changes fromSaturday’s stalemate with Everton, Iraola made 10 from a similarlydrab draw against Fulham. It was new faces but a similar story for Spurs as, for the second successive game against Merseyside opposition, they seized control from the start but failed to capitalise when in the ascendancy. Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus both should have scored from left-wing crosses by Destiny Udogie. The former allowed Mamardashvili to make an ­important, improvised save when he had the entire goal to aim for. The latter volleyed over from four yards out.Liverpool turned the tide thanks to impressive contributions from the young quartet of Lewis Koumas, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha. Koumas led the line with an aggression and work rate that Iraola wants from all of his forwards, regardless of their price tags.Mac Allister opened the scoring when Udogie’s attempt to halt Ngumoha’s weaving run across the area put the ball on a plate for the incoming midfielder. Opening his body, Mac Allister went for power and placement and swept a shot into Martin Dubravka’s top left-hand corner.View image in fullscreenLiverpool’s Alexis Mac Allister fires past Martin Dubravka to open the scoring.Photograph: Scott Heppell/ReutersMac Allister’s opener arrived between Spurs’ two missed chances from Bergvall and Kudus. Another fine Liverpool move and emphatic finish punished the visitors a second time nine minutes after the restart. McConnell and Ngumoha were heavily involved before Milos Kerkez picked out Mac Allister in space, prompting groans from the Kop over the full-back’s refusal to shoot. They were quickly silenced as the Argentina international’s first-time pass found Gakpo, who stepped inside a nonexistent challenge from Archie Gray and beat Dubravka with an angled drive.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAll hope appeared to have been lost for Spurs, not that their finishing offered much in the first place, but the stoic backing of their admirable away support indicated ­otherwise. The visitors were handed a lifeline when Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong failed to deal with a Fernandes corner. The goalkeeper missed his attempt to punch clear and Gallagher, left alone at the back post by Frimpong, had the simple task of heading in from close range.Quick GuideRoundup: Bass and Jones Peterborough's shootout heroesShowPeterboroughmoved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory overBarnsleythat followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining.After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.Brentfordemerged from a tense finish againstReadingto book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Mamardashvili made amends in superb style to deny Marmoush an equaliser when the forward’s shot took a slight deflection off ­Ronald Araújo. At the other end Tosin Adarabioyo escaped twice: first with a wayward pass that led to a gilt-edged chance for Szoboszlai, saved by Dubravka, and when Alexander Isak’s cross struck his arm. There was no video assistant referee in operation to correct the decision.Spurs would not escape a third time. In stoppage time, Szoboszlai let Gakpo’s flick roll off his chest before thumping a fabulous shot beyond Dubravka from long range. He celebrated by pointing to his ear, perhaps in response to the criticism his display against Fulham had attracted. The Liverpool vice-captain’s concerns pale in comparison to De Zerbi’s and his toothless team.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupLiverpoolTottenham Hotspurmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Arch Manning apologizes for ‘insensitive’ joke about AI video of ESPN’s Holly Rowe | College football | The Guardian
description: The Texas star had joked about an AI-generated video that depicted Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian slapping Rowe, a college football reporter for ESPN
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The Texas star had joked about an AI-generated video that depicted Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian slapping Rowe, a college football reporter for ESPN
Content: Texas quarterback Arch Manning had joked about an AI-generated video that depicted head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe.Photograph: Alex Slitz/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTexas quarterback Arch Manning had joked about an AI-generated video that depicted head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe.Photograph: Alex Slitz/Getty ImagesCollege footballArch Manning apologizes for ‘insensitive’ joke about AI video of ESPN’s Holly RoweTexas star called clip of coach slapping reporter ‘hilarious’Manning: ‘Nothing funny about it … I need to do better’Rowe posts that she accepts apology, will move forwardGuardian sportTue 15 Sep 2026 15.18 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 15.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTexas’s star quarterback, Arch Manning, has apologized after joking about an AI-generated video that depicted Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian slapping ESPN college football reporter Holly Rowe after last Saturday’s game.Manning had been asked at a press conference on Monday about the social media reaction to the Longhorns’24-23 upset win over No 1 Ohio State. Rowe had attempted to ask Sarkisian a question for the standard postgame interview, but the coach interrupted her and yelled a pair of Texas slogans before walking off.“I’ve seen a few AI edits, that’s about it. I saw an AI edit of Sark’s interview,” Manning said on Monday. “Y’all seen that one? That’s a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe. It’s hilarious.”Arch Manning leads Texas back from 20 points down in fourth quarter to shock No 1 Ohio StateRead moreHis comments were met with laughter in the room. On Tuesday, Manning apologized with a statement on his Instagram story, calling his words and actions “hurtful to a lot of people”.“In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it,” he wrote. “It’s easy to say I didn’t mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for it.“I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward.”Rowe posted a response on Instagram later Tuesday, saying: “Thank you Arch. I appreciate our conversation about this – which will remain private. Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another.”Evan Vieth, the reporter who asked the question in the press conference, apologized on Tuesday for describing Manning’s reaction as “gold” in a post that has more than 27m views on X.“I sincerely apologize for how I chose to present the tweet, and I’ll be more careful going forward, especially when it comes to AI-generated content and how quickly I hit send,” Vieth wrote.Rowe has spent more than two decades as a sideline reporter for ESPN’s college football and college basketball coverage. She has won a Sports Emmy for her reporting and was honored by the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2023 with its Curt Gowdy Electronic Media Award.Earlier in Saturday’s game, Sarkisian had appeared to avoid talking to ESPN reporter Laura Rutledge for the usual half-time interview. Rutledge later said on the broadcast that ESPN had technical issues. When Rowe found Sarkisian after the game and attempted to ask a question, he screamed, “Let’s go, Texas fight! Let’s go, Texas fight!” before adding “Hook ’Em!” and walking off. A Texas spokesperson said ESPN’s technical difficulties played a role in Sarkisian’s response.Manning, the nephew of former NFL stars Peyton and Eli, is in his fourth season at Texas. The Longhorns came back from a 20-point deficit to beat the Buckeyes on Saturday and are the No 1 team in the country entering the third week of the season.Explore more on these topicsCollege footballCollege sportsUS sportsUS sports medianewsShareReuse this content

title: Patrick Mahomes triumphant on NFL return as Chiefs beat up misfiring Broncos | NFL | The Guardian
description: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns in his Chiefs debut, stealing some of the spotlight from Patrick Mahomes
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns in his Chiefs debut, stealing some of the spotlight from Patrick Mahomes
Content: Patrick Mahomes celebrates a Chiefs touchdown on Monday night.Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPatrick Mahomes celebrates a Chiefs touchdown on Monday night.Photograph: Jamie Squire/Getty ImagesNFLPatrick Mahomes triumphant on NFL return as Chiefs beat up misfiring BroncosDenver Broncos 10–31 Kansas City ChiefsChiefs QB throws two TDs on return from torn ACLKenneth Walker III rushes for 173 yards on debutAgenciesMon 14 Sep 2026 23.38 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 11.24 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKenneth Walker III ran for 173 yards and scored two touchdowns on his Chiefs debut, stealing some of the spotlight fromPatrick Mahomesas Kansas City defeated the Denver Broncos 31-10 on Monday night.The big question, even after Mahomes participated in the entire offseason program and every practice of training camp, was how his surgically repaired left knee would hold up nine months to the day since he tore his ACL. He erased many of those doubts when he capped the Chiefs’ opening drive with a 15-yard touchdown run.Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continue“You see that goalline, you’re a football player and you just try and get in the end zone,” Mahomes said after the game when asked if his time on the sidelines had made him more cautious.Mahomes didn’t appear to be affected too badly by the knee, or the brace he wore on it, throwing for 184 yards and two scores while running for another to help the Chiefs snap a three-game skid against the Broncos, who ended Kansas City’s nine-year run as division champs last season.The Josh Allen rollercoaster is up and running again for the new NFL seasonRead moreWalker carried 23 times to finish with the most yards rushing by a Chiefs player since Jamaal Charles ran for 226 against the Colts in 2012, the year before Andy Reid became their coach. The ex-Seahawks star also had three catches for 18 yards.“Against this team, you have to set a tone and [our] offensive line and those running back did that,” said Mahomes.The Broncos, meanwhile, were abysmal on offense in their first game with coordinator Davis Webb calling the plays.Bo Nix threw for 131 yards with an interception and a lost fumble, and the Broncos finished with 176 yards of offense, despite the offseason splash they made by trading a package of draft picks to Miami for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.Waddle had one catch for two yards and had a costly drop on third down. Evan Engram led the Broncos with four catches for 43 yards and their lone touchdown.It was Walker who did most of the running, though. The Super Bowl MVP for Seattle, who signed a three-year, $43.1m deal in free agency, had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half alone, along with a couple of catches out of the backfield.After Mahomes had opened the scoring, the Broncos tied the game on Nix’s 19-yard touchdown pass to Engram, but Walker carried the load as the Chiefs pieced together a 10-play, 80-yard drive late in the half. It ended when Mahomes found Rashee Rice, fresh off a knee injury of his own, and he caromed off a couple of Broncos defenders and into the end zone to make it 14-7 at the break.Then it was Walker’s turn to bounce off a defender, turning a fourth-and-one carry into a 60-yard touchdown run to start the third quarter.The teams traded field goals later in the quarter thanks to big plays by each side: Brandon Jones intercepted Mahomes deep in Chiefs territory, setting up Wil Lutz’s chip shot, and then Mahomes connected with Travis Kelce for 59 yards to set up Harrison Butker’s field goal.Nix’s fumble on the ensuing possession allowed the Chiefs to put the game away. Mahomes hit rookie running back Emmett Johnson on third down for a 26-yard gain, setting up first-and-goal at the Denver 2. And in the kind of creative play that was reminiscent of the Chiefs’ banner years, Mahomes lined up in a three-point stance alongside backup QB Justin Fields, took the snap and shoveled the ball to Walker, who scooted untouched for the score.Explore more on these topicsNFLKansas City ChiefsDenver BroncosPatrick MahomesUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Louisville’s Savannah DeMelo sues team doctors after cardiac arrest during game | NWSL | The Guardian
description: The midfielder suffered a cardiac arrest mid-game last year, and is alleging negligence on the part of UofL Health and two physicians.
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: The midfielder suffered a cardiac arrest mid-game last year, and is alleging negligence on the part of UofL Health and two physicians.
Content: Savannah DeMelo suffered a cardiac arrest on the field for Racing Louisville last year.Photograph: Steph Chambers/NWSL/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSavannah DeMelo suffered a cardiac arrest on the field for Racing Louisville last year.Photograph: Steph Chambers/NWSL/Getty ImagesNWSLLouisville’s Savannah DeMelo sues team doctors after cardiac arrest during gameMidfielder suffered cardiac arrest mid-game last yearLouisville will drop UofL Health as medical partnerJeff RueterTue 15 Sep 2026 16.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 17.10 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRacing Louisville midfielder Savannah DeMelo has filed a lawsuit against UofL Health and two named physicians for negligence after they allegedly failed to properly diagnose a heart condition before she suffered cardiac arrest in the first half of anNWSLgame on 14 September 2025.According to anscreenshotof the complaint, the filing claims that UofL Health “failed to act as a reasonably prudent and competent medical practice … and such negligence was a substantial factor in causing [DeMelo] to suffer severe physical injuries, including, but not limited to, her cardiac arrest.”Saloons, school and specialty coffee: NWSL players enjoy new era of side hustlesRead moreWhen contacted by the Guardian, a clerk with the Jefferson Circuit Court confirmed that the case was filed on Tuesday morning – a year and a day after her on-field cardiac arrest.Sources close to DeMelo and the club, speaking anonymously due to the sensitive nature of both her recovery and the filing, told the Guardian that Racing has already determined that it will not work with UofL Health after the current season. Neither named physician – including one listed on the club’s website as chief medical officer – is an employee of the club, instead working with the team as part of an agreement between the organizations. Racing is already in the process of finding a new medical partner ahead of the 2027 season.The sources also disclosed that DeMelo, whose contract was set to expire at the end of this season, has reached a verbal agreement with Racing to keep her at the club. The deal is pending league approval and could be announced as soon as next week. DeMelo is nearing a return to competitive action, having resumed full training with her teammates this week. A source said the current timeline could have her involved as soon as 25 September’s match, in which Louisville will host the San Diego Wave.A spokesperson for Racing Louisville declined to comment. UofL Health said it was unable to comment on pending litigation. A representative for DeMelo did not immediately reply to a request for comment.DeMelo has spent her entire professional career with Louisville, selected fourth overall in the 2022 NWSL draft. Her progressive approach in midfield and set-piece prowess made her a surprise pick for the United States’ roster at the 2023 Women’s World Cup, becoming the third player in USWNT history to make a World Cup squad without having previously been capped.In late 2024, DeMelo was diagnosed with Graves’ disease, an autoimmune disorder which causes an overactive thyroid. The midfielder disclosed her diagnosis midway through the following season, havingexited a game on 22 March 2025citing dizziness and chest tightness. Six months later, DeMelo collapsed on the field during a game in Seattle. She was the second NWSL player to have a heart scare during a game last season, with Angel City defender Savy King suffering cardiac arrest on 9 May 2025.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Savy King, my heart goes out to her,” DeMelo told ESPN. “I can’t imagine how scared [she was] and what she’s feeling, but we do have very different situations. … Mine was more due to the medication I was on and what my thyroid was doing to my body.”Explore more on these topicsNWSLWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘I loved my time in the FBI but nothing can compare to the NFL’: Charles ‘Peanut’ Tillman on his unlikely career path | NFL | The Guardian
description: The player who invented the Peanut Punch talks about his nomadic childhood, love of Chicago and time as a cop
Author: Gavin Willacy
Headline: The player who invented the Peanut Punch talks about his nomadic childhood, love of Chicago and time as a cop
Content: Charles Tillman played for the Bears for 12 years, helping them reach the Super Bowl in 2007.Photograph: George Gojkovich/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCharles Tillman played for the Bears for 12 years, helping them reach the Super Bowl in 2007.Photograph: George Gojkovich/Getty ImagesGuardian Sport NetworkNFLInterview‘I loved my time in the FBI but nothing can compare to the NFL’: Charles ‘Peanut’ Tillman on his unlikely career pathGavin WillacyThe player who invented the Peanut Punch talks about his nomadic childhood, love of Chicago and time as a copByNo Helmets RequiredTue 15 Sep 2026 10.03 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 17.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDefensive back Charles Tillman played 168 games for his home-town team theChicago Bearsacross 13 NFL seasons. Nicknamed “Peanut” as a child by his mother, he became renowned for the Peanut Punch, where he would whack the ball out of the hands of unsuspecting receivers. After retiring from playing, he spent eight years in the FBI before quitting over the Trump administration’s ICE policies and tactics. Now 45, he spent some of his summer in England, teaching flag football to kids in Liverpool.You went to a dozen schools around the world as a child. Do you share your own experiences when you coach kids now?“Absolutely. I share a great deal because it helped shape me into the person I am today. My dad being in the military and us moving around so much helped my personality. I’m very outgoing and a lot of that stems from my childhood, always being the new kid in school and having to make new friends. So, I talk about those experiences with the kids when it feels appropriate.”When you walked into a new classroom full of strangers did you have to force yourself to be an extrovert?“No, when I tried to make friends or meet new people, it came from a genuine place. I looked at it as another adventure: ‘Oh, wow, I’ve never been to this country or this state before. Let’s learn about northern California. Let’s learn about West Germany.’ I had a chance to see different cultures and how people lived. ‘OK, this is what they do in Texas. This is how they do it in Louisiana.’ I was pretty well-rounded. And it made me comfortable being around so many different cultures and ethnicities. I loved it.”How’s your German?“Not good. When I lived there, I could speak a little, because they taught us it in school and I was young, so my brain retained it. The most German I see now is subtitles in a movie. I haven’t been to any of theNFLInternational Games in Germany yet. But I’ve been to Toronto and Tottenham – and I played at Wembley!”In contrast to your nomadic childhood, you’ve spent most of your adult life in Chicago. What kept you there?“The food! And the people more than anything. When you’re in Soldier Field, and it’s freezing cold, six degrees fahrenheit, they’re third and two, and you’re on the goalline and you look up in the stands, and you want our fans to scream and yell more – and they do – there’s no greater feeling. That was why I stayed. I loved playing in Chicago. I loved our defence. I loved everything about the city. I love the history, that it was one of the original teams, but more importantly the people. We haven’t won any championship since 1985, but we still have some of the most loyal fans, and they’re waiting. I can’t say patiently, but they’re definitely waiting.”You seemed to go quickly from the NFL to theFBI. Did you prepare for that transition when you were still playing?“Once I knew I was done playing, I knew the process would take a little bit of time, with background checks and all the polygraphs. So I’d been quietly preparing for my time in the FBI for about two years, just living my life. I’m not going to say ‘keeping my nose clean’ because I keep my nose clean every day. I didn’t have to do anything special or different. I just waited until I got a call to go to the academy.”You had earned a lot of money in the NFL so had the freedom to do what you wanted.“It’s a good feeling to have, but whether I had money or not, I just wanted to work. I was only 34 years old, which is far too young to retire. Sitting at home all day, doing nothing and playing golf didn’t really seem sexy to me. I wanted to work. That’s how I’m designed, how I conduct myself. So I just got a job like another normal person. It was a normal job, too, for the most part. It was a nine to five. It was just for the FBI.”Which was more exciting – the NFL or FBI?“Well, there’s no greater job than the NFL. I loved my time in the FBI and it’s one of the greatest jobs I’ve ever done. But the NFL is the NFL. There’s nothing that can compare to that. I enjoyed being in front of the camera playing football, but I also enjoyed being in the FBI, doing some pretty cool stuff. It’s apples and oranges. They are totally different: one is flashy and in your face and all about making money, and in the other they’ll save your life and then just disappear. There’s no glory or nothing, it’s just thankless heroes.”View image in fullscreenCharles Tillman knocking the ball out of the hands of Minnesota Vikings receiver Randy Moss in 2004.Photograph: Chicago Tribune/TNSDid you ever feel out of your depth or scared in either job?“I was nervous but never scared. We were well prepared and ready for it. When you start, I was like: ‘What did I get myself into?’ But I always felt like I belonged in both jobs. I was good enough to be in both organisations.”You’re now in England teaching kids a sport they may never have seen in the flesh. How is that?“It’s a challenge, but they have a lot of fun and, by the end of the day, they’re very intrigued. Liverpool and the Bears have a pretty good relationship and it’s growing: there were more kids than last time I came. I’m helping them learn how to run a route, how to run the football after they catch it, how to throw. Flag football is the easiest way to get the premise of American football. My daughters play it and love it.”Umyla Hanley was working as a builder two years ago. Now he hopes to play for England at a World CupRead moreEveryone thinks NFL players are all giants but wide receivers and cornerbacks can be average-sized people. “They’re normal, but they do extraordinary things with their bodies. They can bend and turn corners and catch footballs that quarterbacks throw from 80 yards down the field. And they are incredibly fast. The beautiful thing is everybody can play flag football. You can be a big kid, a small kid, tall kid, short kid, heavier kid, a very light kid. I absolutely love that.”Does college football prepare players for the NFL – howdo you cope with the leap in standard?“You take the leap and accept the challenge. The really good players love to compete. I was excited, anxious, happy, nervous. You’re a bunch of things at one time but, more importantly, you’re up for the challenge. I didn’t shy away from it and I didn’t mind asking older guys for help. One of my mottos is: you’re either green and growing or ripe and rotting. I wanted to keep growing and never stop learning. Each year, I got smarter. Some of it was just on my own, but a lot of it was from coaches and watching other players. If you ask for assistance, you’ll get it from an NFL player. Guys don’t want to keep the secrets to themselves. They want to give you the knowledge. You just have to be willing to ask for help.”What do we not see from the outside as fans?“One of my big strengths was mental focus, my ability to be dialled in. But I can remember some games when I just wasn’t in the right headspace. I was thinking about stuff at home, say, if one of my kids was sick. But I also had to perform my job on the field. Balancing the two was a challenge sometimes. For us athletes, life happens. People tend to forget that. Personal life plays such a big role in who we are as people, and you never want to bring it to work, but sometimes it affects your business. You’re trying to wear two different hats but we’re human beings.”Explore more on these topicsNFLGuardian Sport NetworkChicago BearsFBIUS sportsinterviewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: The highly regarded 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave a day before he was to be included in Manchester United’s squad to face Brighton
Author: Dominic Booth
Headline: The highly regarded 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave a day before he was to be included in Manchester United’s squad to face Brighton
Content: JJ Gabriel training with Manchester United’s first team this month.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJJ Gabriel training with Manchester United’s first team this month.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedManchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave15-year-old wants his registration to be cancelledHe was to be in squad to face Brighton on WednesdayDominic BoothTue 15 Sep 2026 10.18 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester United have been left confused and shocked by the news that the talented 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave the club, a day before he was to be included in the first-team squad to face Brighton.Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.Are Manchester United as poor as the early Premier League table suggests?Read moreUnited are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.United believe the situation, first reported bythe Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.Gabriel, who has been with United since the age of 11, has emerged as one of the most exciting prospects at Carrington in years, scoring a hatful of goals for the youth teams, most recently a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut against Sabah last week. He regularly plays for older age groups at United, scoring 26 goals in 29 games last season, and has made two appearances for England Under-17s. Gabriel is also the most recent, and youngest, winner of United’s prestigious Jimmy Murphy young player of the year award. He has regularly trained with the first team.Quick GuideCarrick say VAR blunder will fuel UnitedShowMichael Carrick believes Manchester United will have an edge against Brighton in the Carabao Cup owing to the wrong video assistant referee decision that allowed Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s defeat by Manchester City.United host Fabian Hürzeler’s side on Wednesday aiming to bounce back after Haaland’s 60th-minute strike was judged to be legal by the VAR, who ruled that Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup. Pro Ref admitted the goal should not have been allowed and that Matt Donohue, the VAR, had made the wrong decision. He has been stood down for this weekend's Premier League action.Carrick, speaking before Pro Ref’s statement, was asked whether his players would have an edge against Brighton owing to their annoyance at ruling.“It does give you something, when something like that happens, to use moving forward," the manager said. "The players have got an edge. They've shown that to me since I've been here. We've had setbacks, and they've bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results."United have taken  four points from their first four games. “We've got to move on [from City loss]; we've got to win games,” said Carrick. “We have done – we've won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that. I understand it's a new season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be. I'm not hiding from that, but it's more of about getting back to winning games, that feeling, getting the habit. It's easier said than done, but we're capable of it.”Luke Shaw may be available after a knock.Jamie JacksonWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Speaking after that 5-0 win against Sabah, Adam Lawrence, United’s lead under-21 coach, said: “JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through. He’s been at the club for so long. He’s got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well.“At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it’s about making sure that he’s getting the right exposure across different levels. We’re obviously not perfect but it’s definitely something we put a lot of thought into.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBarcelona and Manchester City have been linked previously with Gabriel, after reports emerged last year suggesting the player’s family would be planning to move him.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitednewsShareReuse this content

title: Sophie Cunningham says she spoke to Adam Silver about next WNBA commissioner | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has discussed the soon-to-be vacant WNBA commissioner’s job with Adam Silver after he reached out to her
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has discussed the soon-to-be vacant WNBA commissioner’s job with Adam Silver after he reached out to her
Content: Sophie Cunningham’s Fever are preparing to return after a break during the Fiba World Cup.Photograph: Marc Lebryk/APView image in fullscreenSophie Cunningham’s Fever are preparing to return after a break during the Fiba World Cup.Photograph: Marc Lebryk/APWNBASophie Cunningham says she spoke to Adam Silver about next WNBA commissionerCathy Engelbert is leaving her post at end of yearNBA commissioner often speaks to players about issuesSign up for the free WNBA 30 weekly newsletterAssociated PressTue 15 Sep 2026 12.56 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 13.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIndiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has discussed thesoon-to-be vacant WNBA commissioner’s jobwith Adam Silver after the NBA commissioner reached out to her.“I have talked to Adam Silver a couple times, and I think he’s a great guy,” Cunningham said on Monday. “He was very knowledgeable and full of wisdom and so getting to talk to him and hear his perspective of how he approaches the NBA is huge, who he’s kind of looking for. I think if you want to know the real answers, you go to him.Cathy Engelbert’s WNBA tenure: the wins and losses that defined her seven yearsRead more“But I think he’s going to put someone in place who really wants to take our league to another level than it’s already at. Our league is booming, so why would we not [want] someone who’s going to make it even more booming?”Cathy Engelbert recently announced she would retire from her post asWNBAcommissioner at the end of the year. Silver has a long history of speaking with players about various league topics, though the NBA declined to specifically address what Silver and Cunningham discussed.Cunningham, however, was more outspoken about what she wants to see in the WNBA’s next leader, though she didn’t share names of any candidates she might have in mind.Cunningham has emerged as a polarizing playerthis season because of her position against transgender athletes competing in women’s and girls sports. She has not backed down from her opinion despite backlash from many fans.But Cunningham believes the league needs a unifier.“I think the WNBA has always been a place for people to feel safe and comfortable. I think there’s all types of walks in this organization, or in this league, which I think is absolutely awesome,” Cunningham said. “But I do think with that you need someone who’s going to unite everybody because it can be so different. But that doesn’t mean it’s a bad thing. I think it makes it a lot of fun.”She also wants someone committed to helping the league continue to grow. The WNBA has seen interest in the league soar in recent years, even amid criticism of how Englelbert has handled some off-court issues. On the flip side, Engelbert’s accomplishments include signing a new, richer television contract, a new collective bargaining agreement and adding charter flights for teams.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRegardless of the fans or the critics, Cunningham insists she wants the WNBA to continue its overall mission.“You continue to have a growth mindset and see other people’s walks of life and really get to know why they are the way they are, and I think that’s truly fun,” she said. “Like you are playing the best basketball, you’re in the best league in the entire world and you’re getting to learn so much about who you are as a human, how other people are as a human. But with all that, with all the diversity you do need someone who’s going to unite our league and have a common goal and get us all on the same page. I think that’s super important.”Indiana are waiting for All-Stars Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston and coach Stephanie White to rejoin the team. The trio were part of the United States’ gold-medal winning World Cup team in Berlin. The Fever resume play on Friday at Toronto.Explore more on these topicsWNBAIndiana FeverBasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: USMNT roster prediction: a big chance for Cavan Sullivan and other young prospects | Mauricio Pochettino | The Guardian
description: The United States’ next World Cup cycle gets underway with this week’s squad selection – here’s who we think will make the cut
Author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
Headline: The United States’ next World Cup cycle gets underway with this week’s squad selection – here’s who we think will make the cut
Content: The US play friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.Photograph: Kohjiro Kinno/Sports Illustrated/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe US play friendlies against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.Photograph: Kohjiro Kinno/Sports Illustrated/Getty ImagesMauricio PochettinoUSMNT roster prediction: a big chance for Cavan Sullivan and other young prospectsThe United States’ next World Cup cycle gets underway with this week’s squad selection – here’s who we think will make the cutPablo Iglesias MaurerandJeff RueterTue 15 Sep 2026 07.30 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 07.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGoalkeepersPablo: Matt Turner (New England Revolution), Brian Schwake (Nashville SC), Chris Brady (Chicago Fire), Diego Kochen (Lyngby)Jeff: Turner, Schwake, Kochen, Andrew Thomas (Seattle Sounders)Pochettino’s ‘different’ vow to the US invites unwelcome speculationRead moreMaurer:This is probably the easiest position on the field to predict, but that’s not necessarily a good thing. Turner seems likely enough to retain his starting role for the time being, though Kochen’s age (20) and form seem likely to earn him minutes this window, given Pochettino’s insistence that he wants to use this window to season several Olympic hopefuls. I’d be shocked not to see Schwake in the picture; he has been lights-out for the presumptive Supporters’ Shield winners. Pochettino did mention Nashville last week in a list of players producing promising young talent – at 25, Schwake doesn’t quite fit that descriptor, though as a rule, US keepers tend to skew a bit on the elderly side. Otherwise, I have no idea who on earth Poch could be talking about.Rueter:Turner is the only returnee from the World Cup trio thanks to his excellent record in MLS, leading all goalkeepers with 10.7 goals prevented (per FotMob). Andrew Thomas (9.6) and Brian Schwake (8.2) rank second and fourth in that metric with Seattle and Nashville. Both are mid-20s alternatives to Matt Freese with success at the club level, with Thomas having won the Leagues Cup final over Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami and Schwake having backstopped Nashville to the U.S. Open Cup. Brady’s positioning leaves plenty to be desired with Chicago, while Diego Kochen began the World Cup as a training goalkeeper and is now getting regular games on loan with Lyngby.View image in fullscreenChris Richards will enter as the leader of the US’s defensive unit.Photograph: Silvina Brodersohn/CameraSport/Getty ImagesDefendersMaurer:Chris Richards (Crystal Palace), Tim Ream (Charlotte FC), Neil Pierre (Philadelphia Union), Justin Che (Red Bull New York), Auston Trusty (Celtic), Antonee Robinson (Fulham), Alex Freeman (Villarreal), Tim Weah (Marseille), Max Arfsten (Middlesborough), Peyton Miller (New England Revolution),Rueter:Tristan Blackmon (Vancouver Whitecaps), Luca Bombino (Stoke City), Alex Freeman, Neil Pierre, Tim Ream, Chris Richards, Antonee Robinson, Tim WeahUSMNT to face Mexico and Canada in friendlies to kick off 2030 World Cup cycleRead moreRueter:Robinson (left) and Freeman (right) should enter this cycle as the presumptive starters on their respective sides of the defensive line. Their alternative on each side also considers where each is at in their career: Robinson is 29 and a younger backup should be identified soon, so I’m going with Luca Bombino, who earned a move to Stoke City on the back of his breakout with San Diego FC. Bombino has been comfortable operating as a left back in a back-four, dependable in his positioning and a lesser factor for chance creation than most modern wide defenders. Freeman is the rising option where a more veteran alternative makes sense, and Marseille captain Tim Weah should remain part of this core regardless of a disappointing World Cup. All of his starts this season have come as the right back in a back four.Centrally, Richards enters this cycle with clear status as the defensive bedrock, and Auston Trusty larged fared well this summer. Tristan Blackmon struggled to acclimate in a September crash-course, but has continued to perform at a high level as the lead defender in a possession-dominant Vancouver Whitecaps.Maurer:Ream – the oldest player in USMNT history to appear at a World Cup – would seem easy enough to leave off of this (and future) rosters but he has said he won’t retire international until he retires completely, and Pochettino clearly values him. I also believe he’ll prove a useful tutor to players like Miller, Pierre and Che as they get their footing with the national team. Though Pierre’s composure on the ball remains suspect (a potential issue given how Pochettino likes to play) a 6ft7in, 18-year-old prospect will likely prove irresistible to a program that badly needs help in central defense.View image in fullscreenCavan Sullivan scored twice for the Union against San Diego on Sunday.Photograph: Orlando Ramirez/Getty ImagesMidfieldersMaurer:Tyler Adams (Bournemouth), Sebastian Berhalter (Middlesbrough), Adri Mehmeti (Red Bull New York), Aidan Morris (Middlesbrough), Yunus Musah (Milan), Gio Reyna (Strasbourg), Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union)Rueter:Tyler Adams, Sebastian Berhalter, Gianluca Busio (Venezia), Adri Mehmeti, Aidan Morris, Yunus Musah, Gio Reyna, Cavan Sullivan, Malik Tillman (Bayer Leverkusen), Niko Tsakiris (San Jose Earthquakes)skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMan City-bound 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is MLS’s chaotic revelationRead moreMaurer:In the course of two months Sullivan has gone from a maybe, to a certainty, to looking like he could contribute for the US immediately (though I disagree withhis assertionthat he would have made a difference against Belgium – sorry, kid). His remarks and Pochettino’s ensuing reply to them in the media (though he didn’t name Sullivan directly) convinced me of one thing: that Poch is watching, and perhaps providing a little early guidance for a very useful player. Musah has become a regular contributor for Milan this season – in large part due to the club’s injury issues elsewhere – I for one would love to see him retain his form and would welcome him back.Rueter:McKennie has been sidelined through injury, but Adams has gradually increased his workload early in Bournemouth’s season and has a clear role to own at the base of midfield. However, a minutes limit may be wise. Mehmeti, 17, enters as the apprentice to Adams, although his approach to defensive midfield is far less physical.Busio has thrived in his Serie A return, now captaining Venezia at age 24. His combination of on-ball facilitation, comfortably drifting throughout the midfield to impact a game, and ability to play the final ball makes him a natural alternative in the free-roaming role that Tillman thrived in this summer. Tillman was arguably the team’s player of the World Cup, and his assist on Leverkusen’s equalizer this weekend suggested it’s still worth running things through him. Sullivan has arguably been the best player in MLS – of any age or nationality – since play resumed in July. Tsakiris wasamong MLS’s standout playersbefore his late-spring injury, and his playmaking would be a boost in this pool.View image in fullscreenRicardo Pepi has become a regular at PSV.Photograph: Lars Baron/Getty ImagesForwardsMaurer:Folarin Balogun (Monaco), Zavier Gozo (Crystal Palace), Julian Hall (Red Bull New York), Ricardo Pepi (PSV), Christian Pulisic (Milan)Rueter:Folarin Balogun, Sergiño Dest (PSV), Zavier Gozo, Julian Hall, Ricardo Pepi, Quinn Sullivan (Philadelphia Union), Alex ZendejasIn Zavier Gozo, Crystal Palace land a US prospect living up to the hypeRead moreMaurer:We have yet to get a look at Balogun this year at Monaco, but his inclusion seems as certain as ever, and the empath in me wants to see him thrive with the US after his aborted transfer to Everton and all of the drama that accompanied it. Hall, once the preferred hype vehicle for any number of US fans, has fallen off a bit this year at Red Bull (perhaps understandably, given the fact that he is, you know, a teenager) but remains a promising contributor regardless and seems a certain Olympic selection, if he remains healthy.Rueter:Yes, I omitted Christian Pulisic, who is still slowly getting back to involvement at Milan. More time to train under Amorim and get back to fitness ought to be the priority. Dest was again a liability in defense at a World Cup, this time most glaringly against Belgium, and keeping him further upfield may be necessary for a team with a thinner defensive corps.Gozo isa tricky on-ball operatorwho’s capable of setting up his own shot wherever he receives the ball. A natural option at the thinner right wing, the 19-year-old could offer greater scoring threat from wide areas than Pochettino has enjoyed in his tenure to date. Quinn Sullivan isn’t just here as his brother’s keeper. The 22-year-old was among Pochettino’s best players at the Gold Cup and a World Cup hopeful before his September ACL tear, and is already contributing to Philadelphia’s attack.Pepi is still a regular goalscorer for dominant PSV, although his performances for the national team still leave much to be desired beyond his hold-up chops.Explore more on these topicsMauricio PochettinoUSAUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Max Dowman doubles up for Arsenal’s back-ups to beat Ipswich in Carabao Cup | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Two mesmerising goals in a man-of-the-match display from Max Dowman underlined why the 16-year-old has been compared to a certain Lionel Messi by his manager, Mikel Arteta, as Ipswich were swatted aside with ease
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Two mesmerising goals in a man-of-the-match display from Max Dowman underlined why the 16-year-old has been compared to a certain Lionel Messi by his manager, Mikel Arteta, as Ipswich were swatted aside with ease
Content: Max Dowman (right) scores Arsenal’s third goal – his second – at Ipswich.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAView image in fullscreenMax Dowman (right) scores Arsenal’s third goal – his second – at Ipswich.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PACarabao CupMax Dowman doubles up for Arsenal’s back-ups to beat Ipswich in Carabao CupEd Aaronsat Portman RoadTue 15 Sep 2026 17.14 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 19.18 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe bad news for everyone else is that Arsenal’s next generation is already here. Two mesmerising goals and an assist in a man-of-the-match display from Max Dowman underlined why the 16-year-old has been compared to a certain Lionel Messi by his manager, Mikel Arteta, as Ipswich were swatted aside with ease. Almost as impressive was the performance of the 17-year-old Marli Salmon, who oozed class in central defence on only the second senior start of his career.Ipswich won here the lasttime these two sides met in this competition, in 2011, but were beaten 3-0 in the second leg of the semi-final at the Emirates beforeArsenal infam­ously lost to Birminghamin the final. ­Fifteen years on, Gary O’Neil’s heavily rotated side stood no chance against last year’s runners up after Dowman’s brilliant opening goal. Noni Madueke and the stand-in skipper Mikel Merino were also on target as Arsenal made it seven wins out of seven to start the new campaign. Having finally ended their long wait for silverware in style, this team are hungry for more and know they can now rely on one of the most exciting talents ever to have emerged from their Hale End academy.Szoboszlai screamer seals Liverpool’s progress as De Zerbi’s Spurs woes growRead more“He can deliver those actions effortlessly. That’s his biggest quality,” said Arteta of the delightful shimmy that preceded Dowman’s first goal. “It’s a joy to have him. But what we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context. We really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he’s in the right context with the right ­preparation. That’s what we are ­trying to do.”Both managers made their prior­ities clear as there were a combined 19 changes from their sides’ wins in the Premier League at the weekend. After a summer of heavy spending, many of those who helped Ipswich bounce straight back from the Championship last season were given an opportunity to stake a claim but largely failed to do so. “It’s the most extreme test that you can face,” admitted O’Neil. “Every time we made a mistake we were punished.”Dowman’s most recent first-team appearance was in the final game of last season when Arsenal were crowned champions, and he has since completed his GCSEs before spending a week in New York during the World Cup where he rubbed shoulders with Paul Pogba.Arteta said beforehand he would have “earn his minutes” like anyone else and it only took seven of them for Dowman to seize his opportunity. Ipswich’s fans were taunting their Arsenal counterparts about never being crowned European champions when he muscled Santiago Núñez off the ball on the halfway line and set off towards the penalty area. The imposing figure of Cédric Kipré – all 6ft 3in of him – was all that stood in Dowman’s way but he went past the Ivory Coast defender in a flurry of feet before cooly dispatching a shot into the corner and performing a Thierry Henry knee slide for good measure.Quick GuideRoundup: Bass and Jones Peterborough's shootout heroesShowPeterboroughmoved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory overBarnsleythat followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining.After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.Brentfordemerged from a tense finish againstReadingto book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Ipswich’s mission got even harder when Madueke hammered in after Bruno Guimarães and Merino had combined to set him up after Dowman had started the press. Barely a quarter of an hour had been played. To their credit, the hosts rallied and it needed a clearance off the line from Salmon to deny Zian Flemming. Not to be outdone by Dowman, Salmon – who signed his professional contact when he turned 17 last month having also played in the Champions League and FA Cup last season – set out on a slaloming run just before half-time after calmly turning his way out of trouble under pressure from Flemming, drawing a round of applause from the Arsenal bench.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenThe former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom scores Ipswich’s second goal.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesIpswich’s hopes of mounting a comeback were extinguished within two minutes of the restart when Dowman struck again. Martín Zubimendi’s pass found him on the edge of the six-yard box and the finish was caressed into the far corner. Merino then curled home off the post from Dowman’s touch to put the result beyond any doubt, although the biggest roar of the evening came when Ipswich hit back through Anis Mehmeti after he was set up by the substitute Jack Clarke.Including Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 19 and surely in line for an England recall this week after an excellent start to the season – Arsenal had four teenagers on the pitch at the end after the 18-year-old Theo Julienne came on at right-back. Even Ipswich had a Hale End grad­uate in their ranks by then as Chuba Akpom grabbed another consolation in injury time via a deflection. But, not for the last time one suspects, it was Dowman’s name that was on everyone’s lips at the end.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupIpswich TownArsenalmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Oscar Bobb takes Fulham past stubborn West Ham and into Carabao Cup last 16 | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Oscar Bobb came off the bench to score the winner against an under-strength West Ham, as Fulham won 3-2 in the Carabao Cup
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Oscar Bobb came off the bench to score the winner against an under-strength West Ham, as Fulham won 3-2 in the Carabao Cup
Content: Oscar Bobb celebrates scoring Fulham’s third goal at West Ham.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenOscar Bobb celebrates scoring Fulham’s third goal at West Ham.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PACarabao CupOscar Bobb takes Fulham past stubborn West Ham and into Carabao Cup last 16Jacob Steinbergat London StadiumTue 15 Sep 2026 16.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleÁlvaro Arbeloa played in some great defences but whether he knows how to coach one remains to be seen. ­Fulham have been fragile since appointing the Spaniard and they were fortunate not to be dragged into a penalty shootout by West Ham as this entertainingCarabao Cup tie drew to a close.West Ham equalised twice during the first half and they almost did it again after Oscar Bobb made it 3-2 in the 78th minute. Nuno Espírito Santo raged at a poor miss from Taty ­Castellanos, though, andFulhamclambered into the last 16 after resisting late pressure from the ­Championship pacesetters.It was a mixed bag as far as ­Fulham were concerned. West Ham were beaten but not outplayed and will not mind switching focus back to their promotion push. They stretched Fulham. Arbeloa played an experimental lineup and the performance was not convincing. César Palacios finished with a goal and an assist but Kevin and Emile Smith Rowe disappointed and the Premier League side needed Bobb and Josh King to make the difference after coming off the bench.“I was a bit upset at half-time,” Arbeloa said. “I am asking how we can concede these two goals. So easy for me. We need to improve there. We need to be more aggressive when defending. In the end we need a massive save. If we are not aggressive enough it is my job to improve my players. We have to work a lot.”Ipswich Town v Arsenal: Carabao Cup third round – liveRead moreBefore kick-off there was a moving tribute to Ludek Miklosko, the legendary former West Ham goalkeeper, after he passed away this week at the age of 64. It added emotion to the tie, ensuring the hosts were not short of motivation against the hardest side they have faced since last season’s relegation.Although West Ham rested key players in attack before visiting ­Millwall on Saturday they responded well after going behind in the 13th minute. They tested Fulham in the air and levelled when Arne Engels’ deep cross found Konstantinos Mavropanos, who rose at the far post and headed across for his fellow defender Morato to nod in his first goal since joining from Nottingham Forest on loan this month.View image in fullscreenPablo made it 2-2 just before half-time but West Ham could not find a winner after the break.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAIt was frustrating for the visitors not to maintain control after Palacios darted down the left before picking out Rodrigo Muniz, who headed in the opener after creeping between Mavropanos and Maximilian Kilman.Fulham’s grip remained tentative. Arbeloa had gambled by making nine changes, a risky move after calming the noise around his position with Saturday’s draw at Liverpool. The lead was regained in style, Joachim Andersen’s pass from deep allowing Palacios to wander through a big gap and poke past Finlay Herrick, but Fulham were not resilient enough.
