Their pressing was uncoordinated and it was 2-2 when Benjamin Lecomte’s save from Mohamadou Kanté’s flick ran to Pablo, who marked his 22nd appearance for West Ham by scoring his first goal since joining for £18.3m last January.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideRoundup: Bass and Jones Peterborough's shootout heroesShowPeterboroughmoved into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009 thanks to a 7-6 penalty shootout victory overBarnsleythat followed a thrilling 3-3 draw between the two League One sides.Barnsley were handed the lead after 61 seconds when a clearance by the Peterborough goalkeeper, Alex Bass, was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca’s cross was pushed out by the Barnsley goalkeeper, Kieran Flavell, as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills’ free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod. But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties with by heading in Mills’ cross with just two minutes remaining.After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley’s Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.Brentfordemerged from a tense finish againstReadingto book their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 2-1 victory. Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off. Paudie O’Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading’s challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although the substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.With the game in the balance Nuno made a bold move by introducing Jarrod Bowen and Manor Solomon early in the second half. Fulham drifted. Antonee Robinson drew a save from Herrick but Solomon and Mavropanos went close for West Ham.Arbeloa threw on Bobb, King and Gonzalo García. West Ham tired and King was alert when Kanté dithered in a dangerous position. The Fulham youngster pressed to win possession, leaving Bobb to cut in from the right and drill a low shot past Herrick.West Ham kept going. Bowen shot over and Castellanos, on for Pablo, had an effort cleared off the line by Timothy Castagne. Fulham lived on the edge.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupWest Ham UnitedFulhammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Raheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxide | Raheem Sterling | The Guardian
description: Ex-England footballer pleads guilty and admits to failing to provide a specimen as he appears in court
Author: Sam Cunningham
Headline: Ex-England footballer pleads guilty and admits to failing to provide a specimen as he appears in court
Content: 1:50Bodycam footage shows Raheem Sterling's arrest for dangerous driving – videoRaheem SterlingRaheem Sterling could face prison for reckless driving while using nitrous oxideEx-England footballer pleads guilty and admits to failing to provide a specimen as he appears in courtSam CunninghamTue 15 Sep 2026 09.39 EDTFirst published on Tue 15 Sep 2026 09.35 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRaheem Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and could be sent to prison after driving his ­Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide.The former Chelsea and Manchester City forward stood in the dock to accept three charges before­Basingstoke magistrates court heard how he embarked on a ­prolonged period of reckless driving on the M25 and M3, inhaling nitrous oxide ­balloons, before crashing his £270,000 car. Sterling was disqualified from driving and bailed until 25 November, when his sentence will either be determined or referred to the crown court.Sterling also admitted possession of nitrous oxide and refusing to ­provide a specimen.The maximum term for Sterling would be two years in prison, although a sentence of 12 to 18 months is considered more likely and, with mitigation, that could be suspended.Simon Jones, prosecuting, told the court one witness had “genuine concerns the driver might kill someone” and described Sterling’s driving as “absolutely horrendous”.“As she moved past the vehicle she thought the airbag had been deployed, it was a large white deflated balloon,” Jones said. “She had no idea if the driver could see ahead.”View image in fullscreenRaheem Sterling (centre) arriving at Basingstoke magistrates court on Tuesday.Photograph: Andrew Matthews/PABetween 7.45am and 8.52am on 28 May, police received multiple calls reporting dangerous driving – shortly after Sterling had returned to England after a loan at Feyenoord, where he had attempted to revive his career.Dashcam footage provided to police by one witness showed Sterling’s car swerving between lanes and almost colliding with the central reservation. Witnesses reported seeing the driver inhaling balloons while driving.After leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327 near the Minley interchange in Hampshire. All four tyres blew out and there was damage to the bodywork. Body-worn footage from officers attending the scene, played in court, showed Sterling, 31, sitting in the passenger seat with two canisters on his lap before confirming he had been driving.Jones said Sterling appeared keen to move a deflated balloon from beside him on to the back seat. His saliva was tested and no presence of cannabis or cocaine was found, but he later refused to provide a blood sample to test for other substances.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Another witness told police they had seen the Lamborghini driving erratically at 1.10am. They reported it entering a drive-through at “alarming speed”, Jones said, and saw the driver holding an inflated balloon.After his arrest, Sterling was taken to Basingstoke investigation centre. “During the process he had disclosed to staff that he had a problem with nitrous oxide,” Jones said.Sterling failed a series of impairment tests, including walking in a straight line without swaying and placing his fingertip on the end of his nose. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52.Jones said Sterling “appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting” during the tests. “His eyelids were drooping, consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.”The former England international, who won 82 caps between 2012 and 2022 and played in five major tournaments, was taken to a medical room where he refused to provide a blood sample without providing a reasonable excuse and despite repeated and clear warnings.At 5.13pm, Sterling was interviewed with a legal representative present. A signed, prepared statement was read out in which he said he had not slept all night and was tired and confused. He then answered “no comment” to officers’ questions.Jason Bartfield KC for the defence did not dispute this was a top-category case, given the prolonged driving and clear serious impairment. Bartfield cautioned, however, that there would have been “short periods” of “serious impairment”, compared with consuming cannabis or alcohol.View image in fullscreenRaheem Sterling after being stopped by police in May.Photograph: Crown Prosecution Service/PABartfield did not accept the car damage was serious, describing it as “relatively superficial” and “minor scratching” alongside the blown tyres. He also argued that the fact there were two canisters in Sterling’s lap when police arrived showed “this was very much not a case of trying to conceal anything from them”.The court was not told the full mitigating circumstances, but ­Bartfield said: “Clearly there is extensive ­personal mitigation. Voluntary steps have been taken to address them. I hope this has weight with the court.”District judge Kirsty Allman ordered a pre-sentence report and adjourned the hearing. She said she had not decided whether to retain jurisdiction or commit sentencing to the crown court. A magistrates court cannot impose a sentence of more than 12 months.“I’m going to release you on unconditional bail,” she said. “If you don’t attend, a warrant will be issued for your arrest. I’m going to disqualify you from driving as of today. You must not drive a motor vehicle on the road as of today. I will determine the period if I sentence you, otherwise it will be for the crown court. You must not drive while disqualified – if you drive while disqualified you will be committing a prisonable offence.”Explore more on these topicsRaheem SterlingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Lionel Messi called up by Argentina to make farewell ⁠appearance in friendly | Lionel Messi | The Guardian
description: Lionel Messi has been called up by Argentina to make a farewell ⁠appearance in a home friendly against Benin in October following his international retirement
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lionel Messi has been called up by Argentina to make a farewell ⁠appearance in a home friendly against Benin in October following his international retirement
Content: Lionel Messi after the World Cup final against Spain – his last game for Argentina, unless he accepts a call-up for a friendly in October.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersView image in fullscreenLionel Messi after the World Cup final against Spain – his last game for Argentina, unless he accepts a call-up for a friendly in October.Photograph: Dylan Martinez/ReutersLionel MessiLionel Messi called up by Argentina to make farewell ⁠appearance in friendlyArgentina will host Benin in October in Buenos AiresAFA president invites Messi to enjoy ‘deserved farewell’ReutersTue 15 Sep 2026 18.28 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 18.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLionel Messi has been called up by Argentina to make a farewell ⁠appearance in a home friendly in October following his international retirement, the Argentinian football association (AFA) has confirmed.“We invited ⁠the best player in ⁠the world ​to play, the icon of our selection, our captain Lionel Andrés Messi, to have a deserved farewell on 6 October, here inArgentina,” the AFA president, Claudio Tapia, said on social media.Argentina will play three home friendlies during the 21 September to 6 October Fifa international window, their first matches since the World Cup.They will take on ​Benin in Buenos Aires’ Monumental ‌Stadium on 6 October, ‌where Messi, who announced his retirement from international football last month, has been invited ‌to play his farewell match.Quick GuideRodríguez retires from international footballShowColombia midfielder James Rodríguez retired from international football on ⁠Tuesday, having won 131 caps and inspired his country to the 2014 ⁠World Cup ⁠quarter-finals.“Thank ​you for every match, every joy, every tear and every dream we ⁠shared. Defending the colours of the Colombia national team was one of the ⁠greatest honours of my life,” Rodríguez said in ​a video posted ‌on social media.The ‌35-year-old, who made his senior debut in 2011 ‌and often captained Colombia, scored 31 goals and represented his country at three World Cups and four Copa América tournaments. Rodríguez rose to global prominence at the 2014 World Cup in ‌Brazil, scoring six goals to win the Golden Boot as Colombia reached the ​quarter-finals. His volley against Uruguay in the last 16 earned him Fifa’s Puskas Award for the best goal of the year.He signed for Colombian ⁠side Atlético Nacional last week on a deal ​running ​until next June after ​leaving Major League Soccer club Minnesota ​United.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Argentina will also face Bolivia at Córdoba’s Mario Kempes Stadium on 30 September before moving to Buenos Aires to host Burkina Faso on 3 October. The Bolivia match will be played with capacity reduced by 50% as part of Fifa’s sanctions relating to incidents during this year’s ‌World Cup.“Footballers Messi, [Rodrigo] De Paul and [Giovani] Lo Celso will be in attendance to take part in the final friendly on 6 October. ​Meanwhile, the names of the players called up from the local league will be announced on Friday,” the AFA said in a statement announcing the squad.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionLeandro Paredes, Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada must serve suspensions of 10 matches, seven matches and one match ⁠respectively for their roles in an altercation after theWorld Cup ​final against Spain.Explore more on these topicsLionel MessiArgentinanewsShareReuse this content

title: Howard Webb says accidental handball law ‘a nonsense’ and calls for reform | Laws of football | The Guardian
description: Howard Webb said he wants to stop ‘ridiculous situations’ and that the VAR officials in the Manchester derby had ‘tunnel vision’ over Erling Haaland’s goal
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: Howard Webb said he wants to stop ‘ridiculous situations’ and that the VAR officials in the Manchester derby had ‘tunnel vision’ over Erling Haaland’s goal
Content: Harry Maguire handled the ball and then his off-target shot was deflected in by Jacob Greaves, meaning it counted as an own goal.Photograph: Richard Sellers/Getty Images/AllstarView image in fullscreenHarry Maguire handled the ball and then his off-target shot was deflected in by Jacob Greaves, meaning it counted as an own goal.Photograph: Richard Sellers/Getty Images/AllstarLaws of footballHoward Webb says accidental handball law ‘a nonsense’ and calls for reformWebb wants to stop ‘ridiculous situations’Says VAR officials in United v City had ‘tunnel vision’Paul MacInnesTue 15 Sep 2026 12.59 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 16.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHoward Webb has described the law around accidental handball as “a bit of a nonsense” and called for its reform to stop referees being drawn into “ridiculous situations”.The chief refereeing officer for English football made his remarks on Tuesday, when he also fronted up over the error that allowed Manchester City to win Sunday’s Manchester derby. Webb said he was “really disappointed” with the video assistant referee call that failed to spot Enzo Fernández interfering with play from an offside position beforeErling Haaland scored the only goal.VARs who wrongly confirmed Haaland’s goal at Manchester United are stood downRead moreSpeaking on Match Officials Mic’d Up, Webb reviewed a number of controversial incidents from the Premier League season. He said the buildup to an Ipswich own goal at Manchester United, where the ball hit Harry Maguire’s hand before he took a shot thatdeflected off Jacob Greaves and into the net, highlighted problems with the handball law.“It’s a bit of a nonsense, isn’t it?” Webb said. “If [Maguire] strikes the ball beautifully into the top corner, then the goal gets disallowed. [But] he skews his shot, it becomes an own goal, and it’s awarded.”The handball law says it is an offence “if a player scores in the opponent’s goal directly from their hand/arm [or] immediately after the ball has touched their hand/arm, even if accidental”. If another player touches the ball before it goes in, however, only a deliberate handball would lead to play being brought back. Webb said he believed this was the wrong approach.“The law should change away from that idea,” he said. “We’re in this ridiculous situation whereby the goal is allowed to stand because it’s an own goal. You also get officials having to work out: was the shot on target, was it not on target? The worst-case scenario for us is that the officials decide that the ball is going wide and it’s an own goal, but then later on the goal is attributed to the player that scored, whose arm it hit. So, I think we ought to look at this and just allow the officials to determine whether it’s a normal handball offence. Did he make himself bigger? Did he deliberately handle the ball? And I don’t think [Maguire] does those things in this situation.”Webb, who has promised greater transparency from Pro Ref, is increasingly expected to give a public verdict on controversial decisions and it was not a surprise to find Match Officials Mic’d Up scheduled for TV 48 hours after the farrago in the Manchester derby.View image in fullscreenErling Haaland celebrates after his goal in the derby was cleared to stand.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesThe VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus were stood down from their duties on Monday, after Pro Ref acknowledged “an error of judgment” in assessing City’s winning goal. Donohue was called on to check the decision to disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute strike for offside. Using semi-automated offside technology, Donohue was able to establish that the striker was onside and he overturned ­Oliver’s call. But he failed to spot Fernández had influenced play from an offside position, an ­infringement which Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWebb said it was “important” this error had been acknowledged. “I was really disappointed with this outcome, we all are, none more so than the officials themselves,” he said. “They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they’re obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They’ll not be officiating again until after the international break.”Webb said that Donohue had got “tunnel vision” while assessing the lead-up to the goal, concentrating on Haaland and not Fernández, because the on-field decision was against Haaland. “Donohue doesn’t truly evaluate the full impact of Fernández’s position,” Webb said. “He has a look to see if he touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score. He doesn’t touch the ball, but he doesn’t truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision. He gets focused on Haaland, and it’s down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn’t happen.”Explore more on these topicsLaws of footballHoward WebbRefereesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Craig Bellamy says his loyalty to Wales is unquestionable after rejecting Burnley | Wales | The Guardian
description: Craig Bellamy insisted his commitment to Wales should not be doubted and that he is in ‘the right place for me’
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Craig Bellamy insisted his commitment to Wales should not be doubted and that he is in ‘the right place for me’
Content: Craig Bellamy said that he is in the ‘right place’ as Wales manager.Photograph: Ben Birchall/PAView image in fullscreenCraig Bellamy said that he is in the ‘right place’ as Wales manager.Photograph: Ben Birchall/PAWalesCraig Bellamy says his loyalty to Wales is unquestionable after rejecting BurnleyStaying with Wales over Burnley a ‘simple choice’Never claiming expenses cited as a show of commitmentBen FisherTue 15 Sep 2026 17.44 EDTFirst published on Tue 15 Sep 2026 08.25 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCraig Bellamy said Wales supporters should never question his commitment to the cause after he rejected the chance to manage Burnley, pointing to how he got solicitors’ letters to play for his country and refused to claim expenses on international duty.Bellamy held talks withBurnleyin the summer after the Championship club triggered a release clause in his contract but turned down the move because Wales was “the right place for me”.He spent two years on the staff of Burnley, working as an assistant to Vincent Kompany and taking caretaker charge after the Belgian left for Bayern Munich, describing those years as “heaven”, but declined the chance to succeed Scott Parker.His immediate focus is on Nations League matches against Portugal, Denmark and Norway, the first of which is in Lisbon a week on Thursday. Bellamy said Burnley’s interest posed a quandary but that it was ultimately a “simple” decision to stay withWales, for whom he made 78 appearances as a forward and is under contract until the end of Euro 2028.Quick GuidePlay our football trivia game, On the ballShowThe Guardian'sdaily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.While at Newcastle, Bellamy instructed independent solicitors to enable him to play after his club tried to stop him from featuring in Euro 2004 qualifiers against Italy and Finland. “The club were trying to tell me not to play: ‘[You] can’t play, we’re going to sue you if you do play,’ so I had to get independent solicitors’ letters to make sure I was able to play for Wales,” he said. “I ain’t seen ­anyone else do that.”Bellamy said he had never submitted an expense relating to Wales duty. “Not now, not when I was a player – ever,” the 47-year-old said. “I don’t see it like that. Wales is more important, way more important to me. I charge you for me travelling here? No, I do this for free. I still do now. I’ve never put in an expense, never will.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHe also referenced his donations to Wrexham while a player. “Wrexham going out of the Football League [in 2006-07]? I donate money to Wrexham, they stay in the league,” Bellamy added. “So my commitment with Wales, I don’t believe I have to ever try and win anyone over with that. It’s there [to see], my body of work. I don’t listen to what people say. I always had that gift throughout my career. I mean it in a kind way. I had to so I could have the career I had.”Explore more on these topicsWalesCraig BellamyBurnleynewsShareReuse this content

title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup | Women's football | The Guardian
description: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year
Author: Sophie Downey
Headline: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year
Content: From left: Rachel Maltby, Annika Paz and Celia Segura.Composite: Guardian Picture DeskView image in fullscreenFrom left: Rachel Maltby, Annika Paz and Celia Segura.Composite: Guardian Picture DeskMoving the Goalposts newsletterWomen's footballFrom Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World CupWith an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next yearSophie DowneyTue 15 Sep 2026 08.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 16.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out.Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona)Segura is no stranger to knockout football, having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantle again asLa Rojaeased through their group. Her four goals against New Caledonia were an illustration of her pure scoring instinct and she has also played a key role with her high technical skills and instinctive ability to both make space for and find her teammates. Her back-heel assist to set up Pau Comendador against China was a memorable one. A product of the Barcelona academy, the 19-year-old forward made her debut for the senior side in February and will return to Atlético Madrid for a season-long loan at the conclusion of this tournament.Annika Paz (Argentina and Inter)Paz has taken this tournament by storm with performances that have shown a maturity beyond her 17 years. She is one of a few stars in Poland who have already made their debut for their senior national team – she marked her first cap with a goal against Uruguay in 2025, becoming Argentina’s youngest ever goalscorer. Paz netted four goals against Benin here in Poland before also scoring the opener in Argentina’s dramatic 3-2 win over Mexico to send them through. Her pace, movement off the ball and finishing are exceptional, alongside her composure in front of goal. Having progressed from the River Plate pathway to the senior team, Paz made her move to Europe in January to join Inter.Rachel Maltby (England and Aston Villa)After a breakthrough campaign with Aston Villa last season and now a second youth World Cup with England, it has been a memorable year for Maltby. With her four goals and an assist, the 19-year-old has played a crucial role here in England’s progress to the last 16, as she did at the under-17 edition of the tournament back in 2024, the 19-year-old has caught the eye with her assured, attacking performances down England’s left. Full of energy, composure and with an instinctive ability to time her runs into the box, she has displayed her versatility in switching between her more established full-back role and left wing with ease. Her three penalties, which she can take with either foot, are further examples of how mature she has become over the past 12 months.Annabelle Chukwu (Canada and Notre Dame Fighting Irish)There is plenty of excitement in Canada around this young forward. Chukwu changed the game from the bench with the opening goal in their 1-1 draw with England and then added two more in their 6-0 routing of Tanzania to send her side through to the knockout stage. Pacy and clinical, her direct transitional threat is second to none. The 19-year-old university student has excelled playing for the Notre Dame Fighting Irish and through the national youth pathways. Earning her name as a prolific goalscorer – she broke the record for most goals scored for Canada’s youth teams with 28 in 34 appearances – she received her first senior debut in June and surely has her focus set on being part of Casey Stoney’s side at next summer’s World Cup in Brazil.View image in fullscreenAnnabelle Chukwu of Canada.Photograph: Mateusz Słodkowski/FIFA/Getty ImagesHuang Jiaxin (China and Shanghai Shengli WFC)The centre-back has been one of China’s clear standouts in Poland – not just for her efforts at the heart of the defence but also for her goalscoring ability. Her acceleration up the field and 12-minute hat-trick against New Caledonia illustrated not only her willingness to support her side further up the pitch but also her qualities as an instinctive finisher in front of goal. Her manager, Wang Jun, emphasised this versatility in an interview with Fifa. “She has own characteristics,” he said. “In the future, I hope that she can play in Europe and bring her skills to the senior national team.” At 20, that prospect is not far away, particularly with a World Cup for China on the horizon.Evelin (Brazil and Santos)Given Brazil’s performances in this tournament and with a home senior World Cup to come, it would have been a terrible decision not to include a Brazilian in this list. While there have been quite a few to choose from, the 18-year-old Evelin has particularly impressed. She is small in stature but there is nothing little about her game, with her innate natural ability, energy and eye for a finish. She kicked off the tournament with two almost identical finishes against Tanzania and has also registered two assists to help her team cruise through to the last 16. Domestically, she came up through the ranks at Santos, where she has progressed into the senior setup. She was part of the Brazil team that finished fourth at last year’s Under-17 World Cup and made her senior debut in April 2026.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGet in touchIf you have any questions or comments about any of our newsletters please emailmoving.goalposts@theguardian.com.This is an extract from our free email about women’s football, Moving the Goalposts.
